# Docs Assist

> A Claude Code plugin that coaches subject matter experts through writing documentation.
> It gives Claude Code documentation expertise: guiding contributors through knowledge extraction, picking the right content structure, applying writing standards, and connecting new docs to existing content.

## Docs

- [Docs Assist documentation](docs/README.md): Index of the four reader-facing pages, and which one you want depending on what you are doing.
- [Get started with Docs Assist](docs/get-started.md): Install the plugin, set it up so it writes like your project, and make sure it shows up when it should. Start here.
- [Set up documentation standards for your team](docs/set-up-documentation-standards-for-your-team.md): For docs leads and devrel. Why to install, what changes for contributors, and how to customize.
- [Write docs with Docs Assist](docs/write-docs-with-docs-assist.md): For individual contributors. What the plugin does, and tips for getting the most out of it.
- [Docs Assist command reference](docs/command-reference.md): Every command with its argument and an example.
- [How the authoring loop works](docs/how-the-loop-works.md): What happens when the plugin drafts for you, and why it is built that way. Three reviewers in separate contexts, and the ledger of assumptions you review instead of a whole draft.

## Plugin Configuration

- [SKILL.md](skills/docs-assist/SKILL.md): Core instructions that shape how Claude Code behaves during documentation tasks.
- [Plugin manifest](.claude-plugin/plugin.json): Plugin metadata, version, and registered commands.
- [Marketplace manifest](.claude-plugin/marketplace.json): Marketplace metadata used to install the plugin.

## Commands

- [/docs-assist:health](commands/health.md): Fast docs health check: a scorecard across coverage, freshness, consistency, and findability, plus the single highest-leverage fix. The recommended first command.
- [/docs-assist:draft](commands/draft.md): Write a document through the authoring loop. The contributor brings what they know; the plugin handles the writing.
- [/docs-assist:plan](commands/plan.md): Plan a full documentation set: user journeys, content types, priorities, and writing order.
- [/docs-assist:audit](commands/audit.md): Review existing docs by reconstructing what each one claims and ruling on it. The loop pointed at a finished doc.
- [/docs-assist:verify](commands/verify.md): Verify a procedural doc by executing its steps in an isolated workspace and reporting where the doc diverges from reality.
- [/docs-assist:update](commands/update.md): Find and update the docs affected by a code change (a diff, a PR, or changed files).
- [/docs-assist:release-notes](commands/release-notes.md): Turn a release's worth of changes into reader-facing release notes, leading with breaking changes and upgrade steps.
- [/docs-assist:setup](commands/setup.md): Set up conventions, linting, hooks, and site navigation in one pass. Every stage opt-in, nothing written without a yes.
- [/docs-assist:merge-prep](commands/merge-prep.md): Get a docs change ready to merge. Everything expensive that scales with the whole set runs here and nowhere else.

## Skills

- [docs-assist](skills/docs-assist/SKILL.md): the documentation expert. Intake, the authoring loop, standards, and every reference file the chairs load.
- [writing-task](skills/writing-task/SKILL.md): a wider net. Recognizes work that is documentation-shaped without being called documentation, routes to what fits, and says plainly when the plugin has nothing for it.

## Agents

- [chair-authority](agents/chair-authority.md): The authority chair in the authoring loop. Emits a cold, prose-free packet of what is true, then rules on the ledger entries the advocate chair added. Holds the only web access in the loop.
- [chair-advocate](agents/chair-advocate.md): The advocate chair. Shapes a packet into a document and declares, as a ledger, everything it added that the packet did not contain.
- [chair-continuity](agents/chair-continuity.md): The continuity chair. Reconciles example values, naming, and sequencing against the rest of the set, so a reader working straight through meets something coherent.
- [cold-reader](agents/cold-reader.md): Reads one finished document with no repository access and states what it would do and expect. Divergence names the paragraph at fault.
- [doc-updater](agents/doc-updater.md): Updates a single doc to match a code change. Used to fan out update-on-change across many files.
- [doc-intake](agents/doc-intake.md): Reads a pile of raw source material in isolation and returns a compact content inventory. Used to fan out corpus intake without loading the pile into the main conversation.
- [doc-recon](agents/doc-recon.md): Reads a codebase in isolation and returns a compact project map (what it does, features, entry points, audiences, candidate docs). Used to orient a from-scratch docs effort without reading the whole repo in the main conversation.
- [doc-harvester](agents/doc-harvester.md): Mines issue replies, pull request review comments, and commit message bodies for what maintainers already explained but never documented. Opt-in; returns an inventory, never raw content.
- [doc-verifier](agents/doc-verifier.md): Executes one procedural doc's commands in an isolated workspace and reports, step by step, where reality diverges from the doc. Used to fan out verification across a set's procedural docs.

## Standards and Methodology

- [Knowledge intake](skills/docs-assist/reference/intake.md): Gather before you structure. The dump-first intake loop for one doc, and the corpus content-inventory method for from-scratch work.
- [Content types](skills/docs-assist/reference/content-types.md): The canonical content types and their frontmatter values. The single source of truth.
- [Frontmatter spec](skills/docs-assist/reference/frontmatter-spec.md): Schema for per-doc metadata: fields, tiers, and how the plugin uses them.
- [Tone and voice](skills/docs-assist/reference/tone-and-voice.md): Formatting rules, heading case, markdown style, and voice guidelines.
- [Reference registry](skills/docs-assist/reference/reference-registry.md): The single canonical registry for example values, verified facts, worked-example pointers, and terminology. What each of the four entry kinds is for and how it gets checked, including by a generated Vale rule.
- [Second-opinion pass](skills/docs-assist/reference/second-opinion.md): The silent fresh-reader review every prose-writing workflow runs before showing its output: run cold, briefed with settled facts, once per artifact, mechanical fixes applied silently.
- [User story outlines](skills/docs-assist/reference/user-stories.md): The quick per-doc reader contract (who arrives, from where, to do what, done when what). Drafting writes to it at the shape move; audits walk each story through the doc: arrival, entry, path, exit.
- [Code examples](skills/docs-assist/reference/code-examples.md): Write safe code samples that stay consistent across docs, using the reference registry's example-variable entries.
- [Terminology](skills/docs-assist/reference/terminology.md): Keep product terms consistent across docs, using the reference registry's term entries, which audits check for drift and a generated Vale rule also enforces.
- [llms.txt](skills/docs-assist/reference/llms-txt.md): The llms.txt format, entry ordering, and the maintenance contract every workflow follows. Surfacing docs for AI readers is core functionality.
- [How this plugin gets triggered](skills/docs-assist/reference/triggering.md): What makes the plugin show up and why it sometimes does not, the four surfaces, and what a project can add to change it.
- [Config resolution](skills/docs-assist/reference/config-resolution.md): How a project's committed `.docs-assist/` configuration overrides the defaults and feeds the linters.
- [Documentation patterns](skills/docs-assist/reference/documentation-patterns.md): Patterns, antipatterns, examples, SEO, and accessibility.
- [Templates](skills/docs-assist/reference/templates.md): Suggest and apply external documentation templates (The Good Docs Project) for a healthy start. Opt-in, with content-type and seven-action selection.

## For Docs Leads

- [Audit methodology](skills/docs-assist/reference/audit-methodology.md): Systematic audit process for docs leads.
- [Impact analysis](skills/docs-assist/reference/impact-analysis.md): Scope a change-based audit or update. Maps each change type to the edges it can break, with a traversal budget and residual-risk reporting.
- [IA methodology](skills/docs-assist/reference/ia-methodology.md): Information architecture research, design, and validation.
- [Style guides](skills/docs-assist/reference/style-guides.md): Style guide selection, components, and enforcement strategies.
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): How to contribute to this plugin.
